messages:
sara: Heads up — scheduling a maintenance window for runtime patching and kernel tweak that affects hosted inference (non-blocking for Dedicated but might cause short token-level lat spikes). Target window: 2026-04-03 01:00-02:30 UTC.
eli: Thanks — is this a full rolling deploy or a canary first?
devin: Canary first: 5% traffic in eu-west-1 -> 25% -> full over 45m. We’ll pin critical customers to previous runtime for the first hour if any regressions.
chris: Noted. Can you add the fallback plan for customers on Dedicated who opted out of autoscale? We should tell them to expect a brief reconnect for long-lived streams.
sara: Good call. Add this line to comms: "For Dedicated private pools: streaming sessions >60s may reconnect once; no data loss."
cs-manager: Draft statuspage snippet please — we’ll need one for Scheduled Maintenance (info) and one for Degraded (if we see errors). Keep language non-technical.
devin: Drafted two short snippets below — please edit.

support-bot: ```Scheduled maintenance: We will perform a short runtime update on 2026-04-03 01:00–02:30 UTC. Most customers will see no interruption; some API requests may experience brief latency increases. For Dedicated customers, long-lived streams may reconnect once. Status: Scheduled.```

support-bot: ```If we detect regressions or elevated error rates, we will update status to "Degraded" and pin affected customers to the prior runtime while we rollback. Estimated time to mitigate: 30–60 minutes.```

eli: Those look good. Add a short customer email subject: "Planned maintenance — short window (Apr 3)" and a 1-line hero: "We’re updating our inference runtime to improve stability; you may see brief latencies."
sara: Also include FAQ bullet: 
- Why am I getting reconnects? -> Reconnects are to preserve inference state; no tokens are lost.
- Will my dedicated pool be updated? -> Yes, during the window; you can request to defer via support ticket.

chris: Ops checklist for rollout: 
- create canary job (5%)
- monitor 95p latency and 5xxs for 10m
- promote to 25% if stable
- if 5xx > baseline+0.5% or 95p > baseline+80ms -> hold and pin affected customers
- if pinned customers > 3 -> rollback fully and post incident comms

devin: Rollback plan: switch traffic to runtime 1.8.2 (pinned) and trigger emergency-rollout to ensure cache warm. We’ll also enable quantized-variant q4f-fallback for cost-sensitive routes as a temporary capacity option.
sara: Can someone prepare the customer-facing support template? Keep it short and action-oriented.

cs-manager: Draft support reply for tickets: ```Thanks for the ping — we’re performing a planned runtime update during 2026-04-03 01:00–02:30 UTC. If you experience reconnects or elevated latency, reply here and we can pin your account to the prior runtime until we verify stability. Apologies for any disruption — we’ll update the status page at each step.```

eli: Add internal notes for SRE on-call: escalate to oncall@redwood if pinned-cust > 2 or error budget burn > 20% in 30m.

deploy-bot: deploy 2101234570 canary started in eu-west-1: 5% traffic -> monitoring hooks armed.

sara: Perfect. @cs-manager please queue the email and statuspage posts for 30m before window. @devin please set the rollback alias and pin action in the rollout config.

cs-manager: Queued. Email scheduled T-minus 30 minutes to all active API keys.

devin: Pin/rollback actions set in rollout config and tested locally. I’ll watch metrics during canary.

chris: I’ll stand by for manual rollback if alert fires. :eyes:

sara: Thanks team — will post final pre-window reminder 30m out and update this thread with the statuspage URLs as they go live.

support-bot: Posted scheduled status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/maint-2101234567

sara: Closing the planning thread; we’ll continue live updates during the window in #eng-oncall and post a short customer digest after. :white_check_mark:
